decisions.reason: It has remained on a dedicated page for two years, so without clear negative evidence the option value of waiting for mission uptake still outweighs the low cost of keeping it marketed.
The successful ESA HERA launch is a strong external validation of performance and market relevance, making withdrawal very unlikely.
A second year with its own page indicates continued commitment in a strategically relevant but still uncertain segment, so management would keep the option open.
Being only mentioned rather than fully featured signals weaker commitment, but in a long-cycle space niche the firm can still cheaply preserve this option for another year.
As a 2024 launch with a dedicated page, it is too early to judge its full value, so real-options logic favors continued market presence.
It is very new and only lightly committed on the website, so drop risk is higher, but management would still likely wait for more information before withdrawing it.
